correctness.rationale: Four-channel propensities at (1,1) yield K=[[-10,-q],[1,-1]] and D=diag(20,2). The two exact resolvent spectra follow by 2x2 inversion. The mRNA derivative with respect to omega squared is proportional to P(q)/10-2(1+q^2/10)x-x^2, proving the unique global maximum when P>0. The cubic derivative has just one turning point on the real-eigenvalue domain [0,81/4), and P(0)<0<P(1), P(5)<0, proving exactly two crossings. Protein derivative is negative on that domain. A symbolic checker independently reconstructs the inverse resolvent and derivative identities; 72 numerical resolvent evaluations pass. All assumptions, weak-noise limitation and root endpoint behavior are explicit.

originality.rationale: The distinct assessed statement is an exactly classified reentrant feedback window for the mRNA/controller PSD of a fixed-operating-point two-species negative-feedback reaction network, despite real negative relaxation eigenvalues. The source already supplies the general PSD resolvent; Gupta--Khammash explicitly supplies the two-species NFB protein/output PSD and its peak criterion, and Joo--Chauhan shows real-eigenvalue spectral peaks for three-species networks. Accordingly neither the general PSD method, protein low-pass subclaim, nor real-eigenvalue noise amplification in itself is claimed as novel. Searches and primary comparisons did not identify published explicit mRNA/controller reentrance with the cubic thresholds. Supplementary work and broad formulas remain material implicit-coverage risks.
residual_risks: Gupta--Khammash supplementary Proposition S4.1 or an uninspected general-controller-spectrum extension could implicitly include the mRNA peak classification.
Any broader general OU rational-spectrum theorem may subsume the cubic specialization, even without the same parameter values or title.

The fixed-mean exponential repression curve is a mathematically valid smooth feedback specialization, and its exact numerical thresholds are not universal biological constants.

value.rationale: The model is a two-stage transcription--translation circuit with two experimentally distinct observables and a natural disparity between mRNA/protein turnover. A fully resolved reentrant band-pass window while deterministic modes stay overdamped separates noise-filter resonance from deterministic spiral relaxation, and warns that increasing feedback does not monotonically enhance spectral peaks. The known protein low-pass component emphasizes observable dependence without claiming independent novelty. Exact feedback boundaries and an open-parameter witness give meaningful structural/experimental targets beyond arbitrary spectral arithmetic.
